title: Depreciation and Valuation Methodology for Used Motor Vehicles
summary: The valuation framework for used and reconditioned vehicles evolved from a flat consolidated depreciation rate to a tiered, age-based depreciation structure. Initially, the policy applied a fixed 25% depreciation on the average market value, but this was later replaced by a more granular, progressive scale based on the vehicle's age to better reflect market reality.

evolution.depreciation_model: Transitioned from a flat consolidated rate (25%) to a progressive, age-specific tiered rate.
evolution.eligibility_scope: Expanded the age limit for depreciation eligibility from 3 years to 5 years.

timeline.change: Established a consolidated 25% depreciation rate on the average market value for vehicles up to 3 years old.
Extended the eligibility for the 25% consolidated depreciation rate to vehicles up to 5 years old.
Shifted from a flat 25% consolidated depreciation to a progressive, year-based depreciation schedule for vehicles up to 5 years old.

Motor Vehicle Imports: This instrument establishes a method for determining the customs value of imported used, old, or reconditioned motor vehicles by referencing international valuation journals and applying specific depreciation rates.

The depreciation is calculated by taking the average price from specified valuation journals, deducting a percentage, and applying a consolidated depreciation rate for vehicles within a certain age threshold.
Certificate: To qualify as a used or reconditioned vehicle for valuation purposes, the importer must submit a Registration Cancellation Certificate to the relevant customs office or customs station.
For vehicles imported from Japan, an additional age-related certificate issued by the Japan Auto Appraisal Institute is required as proof of vehicle status.

To qualify as a used or reconditioned motor vehicle for valuation purposes, the vehicle must have a minimum age of one year between its initial registration and cancellation, and it must have been driven for at least a minimum distance.

Importers must submit valid documentation, including the registration cancellation certificate and, in the case of imports from Japan, an age certificate issued by the Japan Auto Appraisal Institute, to the customs station at the time of clearance.
Certificate: A Registration Cancellation Certificate is a mandatory document required for the clearance of imported used or reconditioned motor vehicles.
For vehicles imported from Japan, an additional age-related certificate issued by the Japan Auto Appraisal Institute is required to be submitted to the customs authority.
